mainTopic: Salting offerings: which items need salt, the status of cooked and congealed blood, and how salt is applied
overview: The גמרא first fixes a list by taking out wood and putting in wine libations. It backs this up with a ברייתא saying that wine, blood, wood and קטורת need no salt. That ברייתא fits neither רבי nor the רבנן, so the גמרא says it follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. In his view, an item needs salt only if it can become טמא, is burned in the fire, and is offered on the outer מזבח. The גמרא then asks why a פסוק is needed to exempt blood, since salted blood counts as cooked and is no longer 'blood'. This leads to a discussion of cooked and congealed blood: when eating it still breaks the איסור of blood, the split between outer and inner חטאות, and רבא's and רב פפא's view that congealed blood stays forbidden. A short side topic asks when blood on the skin blocks טבילה. Finally the גמרא returns to the salt פסוק. It explains what kind of salt to use and how to salt a limb: salt both sides, then offer it. אביי adds that the same method works for meat before it goes into a pot.

steps.title: Remove wood and put in wine libations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the earlier list by taking out wood and putting in נסכים (wine libations).
steps.simpleTranslation: Take out wood and put in wine libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it was just dealing with by changing the list: wood comes out, and wine libations go in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood does not belong on this list of items exempt from salt, so the גמרא puts נסכים in its place. The next line brings a ברייתא to back up this swap.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine libations poured on the מזבח
Wood (the logs for the fire on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Remove wood and insert wine libations,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised just before this section by changing the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which items are on the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Wood is taken off the list and wine libations are put on it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: wine, blood, wood and incense need no salt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted to show that wine libations do not need salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: but wine, blood, wood and incense do not need salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to support the swap it just made, since this ברייתא includes wine among the items that need no salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists four items that are exempt from salt: wine, blood, wood and קטורת. It proves that wine belongs among the exempt items. The ברייתא also exempts wood and קטורת, and the next step will ask whose opinion that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt put on items offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: But the wine and the blood,
and the wood and the incense,
do not require salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֲבָל הַיַּיִן וְהַדָּם וְהָעֵצִים וְהַקְּטֹרֶת אֵין טְעוּנִין מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the swap made in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That wine libations do not need salt
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing wine, blood, wood and קטורת as exempt from salt

steps.title: Whose view is this ברייתא? Neither side fits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא. רבי does not fit, because of what it says about wood. The רבנן do not fit, because of what it says about incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is רבי, wood is a problem. If it is the רבנן, incense is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows, and shows that neither of the two known opinions works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that wood needs salt, but the ברייתא says it does not. The רבנן hold that anything which needs another item in order to be offered needs salt. קטורת needs wood to burn, so by their rule it would need salt, but the ברייתא exempts it. The גמרא now needs a third opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; it does not fit

steps.confusionAlert: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא. He holds that wood does need salt, which is the opposite of what the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If it is רבי, wood is difficult,
phrases.notes: רבי holds that wood needs salt, so a ברייתא that exempts wood cannot be his.

phrases.english: If it is the רבנן, incense is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא follows, given that neither רבי nor the רבנן fits it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי requires salt for wood, and the רבנן's rule would require salt for קטורת, yet the ברייתא exempts both.

steps.title: It follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows a third תנא. He learns from the פסוק that salt is needed only for an item that can become טמא, is burned in the fire, and is offered on the outer מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is this תנא. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: The item the פסוק spells out can become impure, is burned in the fire, and is on the outer altar. So too, any item that can become impure, is burned in the fire, and is on the outer altar needs salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows a different תנא, and quotes his rule for which items need salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the method of a פרט: the מנחה that the פסוק names sets the model. Only items that share all three of its features need salt: they can become טמא, they are burned in the fire, and they are offered on the outer מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The specific item the פסוק spells out; here, the מנחה
Goes up onto the fire of the מזבח
The outer altar in the courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-part test is what explains every exemption in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is this תנא,
As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says:
Just as the item that is spelled out
phrases.notes: This means the מנחה named in ויקרא 2:13, "season every מנחה with salt."

phrases.english: is an item that can become impure,
and goes up onto the fire,
and is offered on the outer altar,
so too, any item that can become impure
and goes up onto the fire
and is offered on the outer altar.
phrases.notes: He doesn't say "needs salt" out loud here, but that's what he means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by naming a third תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow either רבי or the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and his three-part test.

steps.title: Why wood, wine, blood and incense are left out
steps.stepSummary: Each exempt item fails one of the three features: wood cannot become impure, wine and blood are not burned, and incense is offered on the inner altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wood is left out because it cannot become impure. Blood and wine are left out because they do not go on the fire. Incense is left out because it is not on the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the three-part test and shows how it exempts exactly the items on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item lacks one feature: wood cannot become טמא, blood and wine are not burned, and קטורת is offered on the inner altar. This matches the exempt list exactly, so the question from step 3 is fully answered.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. An item needs salt only if it can become טמא, is burned in the fire, and is offered on the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: Wood is excluded,
since it cannot become impure,
blood and wine are excluded,
since they do not go up onto the fire,
incense is excluded,
since it is not on the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the test from step 4 to the items on the list.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three-part test exempts wood, wine, blood and קטורת, which matches the ברייתא exactly.

steps.title: Why would we ever think blood needs salt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed to exclude blood from salting. Salting blood turns it into 'cooked' blood, which is no longer treated as blood at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the only reason blood needs no salt that the פסוק excluded it? Without the פסוק, would we really think blood needs salt? Once you salt blood, it stops counting as blood. זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: if someone cooked blood and drank it, he does not break the איסור of eating blood. רב יהודה said in the name of זעירי: if someone salted blood and drank it, he also does not break that איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from the last steps that we need a פסוק to teach that blood does not need salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that salting blood counts like cooking it. Cooked blood loses its status as blood, so it could not be put on the מזבח anyway. So why would anyone think blood needs salt, and why would we need a פסוק to say it doesn't?

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (what we would think without the source)
the status or category of blood
one does not transgress because of it

steps.confusionAlert: Salting here works like cooking. That is why salted blood is treated just like cooked blood.

phrases.english: But is the reason only that the verse excluded blood,
phrases.notes: This points back to the third תנא in step 4, who learned from the פסוק which items need salt.

phrases.english: implying that if not for this,
I would have said that blood needs salt?
Once one salts it,
it leaves the category of blood,
as Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
blood that one cooked, one does not transgress by it,
phrases.notes: He means that drinking it does not break the איסור of eating blood.

phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda said in the name of Ze'eiri:
blood that one salted, one does not transgress by it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the derivation used in steps 4-5 to exempt blood
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a פסוק is needed to exclude blood from salting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salting blood counts as cooking it, and cooked blood loses its status as blood. So nobody would think to salt it, and the exclusion is pointless.

steps.title: Roasted limbs are not a pleasing aroma
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה adds his own ruling: limbs of a קרבן that were roasted before being put on the מזבח do not fulfill 'a pleasing aroma'. This backs up the idea that a cooked offering is no good on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה himself said: if someone roasted the limbs of a קרבן and then brought them up on the מזבח, they do not count as 'a pleasing aroma'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling that strengthens the challenge from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If roasting limbs before the מזבח ruins them as an offering, then 'cooking' blood by salting it would also ruin it. This makes the question stronger: salting blood would harm it, not help it.

keyTerms.meaning: limbs of an offering (usually of an עולה)
he brought them up onto the מזבח
a pleasing aroma to ה׳, a requirement of offerings

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda himself said:
limbs that one roasted and then brought up on the altar,
do not count as "a pleasing aroma."
phrases.notes: שמות 29:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ruling that supports the challenge
steps.raayaObject: The idea that cooking an offering before the מזבח disqualifies it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's own ruling about roasted limbs

steps.title: Maybe a tiny sprinkle of salt for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is still needed. Without it, we might think a tiny bit of salt should be sprinkled on the blood just for the מצוה, since that little would not cook it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that we should sprinkle a tiny bit of salt on it, just to do the מצוה. So the פסוק teaches us that blood needs no salt at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows why the פסוק is still needed to exclude blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large amount of salt would 'cook' the blood. A tiny amount would not. So without the פסוק we might require a small sprinkle as a token מצוה, and the פסוק tells us that even this is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (sets up a mistaken idea)
merely for the sake of the מצוה
it teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק excluding blood from salt is still needed. Without it, we might have required a tiny token sprinkle that would not cook the blood.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let him sprinkle on it any small amount
merely for the מצוה —
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 6-7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the פסוק comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tiny token amount of salt, too little to cook the blood, should be put on it for the מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that blood needs no salt at all, not even a token amount

steps.title: Back to זעירי's rule about cooked blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now focuses on זעירי's rule that cooked blood does not carry the איסור of blood. רבא was teaching this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the main point: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא that if someone cooked blood, drinking it does not break the איסור. רבא was sitting and teaching this rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about זעירי's rule, which was quoted before only in passing. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the rule was used only as a tool for another question. Now the גמרא looks at the rule itself. The note that רבא was teaching it sets up אביי's objection.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא returns to look at a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
blood that one cooked, one does not transgress by it.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָא אָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rava was sitting and teaching this ruling,

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a ruling quoted in step 6 to study it on its own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooked blood loses its status as blood, so drinking it does not break the איסור of eating blood

steps.title: אביי objects: curdled blood still makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא from a ברייתא. Someone who curdled blood and ate it, or melted חלב and swallowed it, is still liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him from a ברייתא: if someone curdled blood and ate it, or melted forbidden fat and swallowed it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the rule that cooked blood is no longer forbidden blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that changing the form of blood, by making it solid, does not take away its איסור. That seems to go against זעירי's claim that cooking blood takes it out of the category of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: he curdled or thickened (made a liquid solid)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
if one curdled blood and ate it,
or melted forbidden fat and swallowed it —
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling restated in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's rule that cooked blood does not carry the איסור of blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that changing blood's form (curdling) does not remove the איסור. So cooking should not remove it either.

steps.title: Fire-curdled versus sun-curdled blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that זעירי speaks of blood curdled by fire, which never turns back to liquid. The ברייתא speaks of blood curdled by the sun, which can turn back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, he curdled it by fire. There, he curdled it by the sun. Blood curdled by fire does not go back to liquid. Blood curdled by the sun does go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends זעירי's rule against אביי's question from the ברייתא. He says the two sources are talking about two different kinds of curdling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood hardened by fire is changed for good, so it is no longer 'blood' and eating it does not break the איסור of blood. Blood hardened by the sun can melt back into liquid, so it is still blood, and the ברייתא makes one liable for it.

keyTerms.meaning: it goes back to its earlier state

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where he curdled it by fire,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is זעירי's rule that cooked blood is not forbidden as blood.

phrases.english: there, where he curdled it by the sun.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ברייתא אביי quoted, which says one is liable.

phrases.english: By fire, it does not go back;
by the sun, it goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן שֶׁהִקְפָּה בָּאוּר, כָּאן שֶׁהִקְפָּה בַּחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources speak of different methods of curdling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to contradict זעירי, because it makes one liable for curdled blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fire-curdled blood can never go back, so it is not 'blood'. Sun-curdled blood can go back, so it stays forbidden.

steps.title: Even sun-curdled blood should be pushed away
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that even sun-curdled blood should be exempt. Once it was unfit for the מזבח, it is pushed away for good, as רבי יוחנן ruled. רבא has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even with the sun, let us say: since it was pushed away, it stays pushed away. For רבי מני asked רבי יוחנן: blood that congealed, and someone ate it, what is the law? He answered: since it was pushed away, it shall stay pushed away. רבא was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer. Sun-curdled blood was unfit for the מזבח while it was hard, so it should lose the status of 'blood' for good, even if it later melts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer relied on the fact that sun-curdled blood can go back to liquid. אביי says that does not matter: once the blood was pushed away from the מזבח, it stays pushed away. רבי יוחנן ruled exactly this about congealed blood, so the ברייתא is still a problem, and רבא cannot answer.

keyTerms.meaning: since it was pushed away (made unfit), it stays pushed away
he was silent, he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pushed away' here means the blood became unfit to be put on the מזבח. Because of that, it is also pushed out of the איסור of eating blood. It does NOT mean the blood becomes more forbidden.

phrases.english: Even by the sun, let us say:
since it was pushed away, it is pushed away,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מָנִי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for רבי מני asked of רבי יוחנן:
Blood that congealed, and someone ate it, what is the law?
He said to him: Since it was pushed away, it shall stay pushed away.
He was silent.
phrases.notes: רבא is the one who goes quiet. He has no answer to אביי.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּחַמָּה נָמֵי לֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִידְּחִי אִידְּחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's fire-versus-sun answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that sun-curdled blood stays forbidden because it can go back to liquid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's principle says that once blood is unfit for the מזבח, it is pushed away for good. So whether it can return to liquid should not matter, and the ברייתא's liability is still unexplained.

steps.title: Outer versus inner חטאות
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests a different way to settle the sources. The ברייתא speaks of outer חטאות, and זעירי speaks of inner חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps, surely, here it speaks of the outer חטאות, and there it speaks of the inner חטאות!
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא is stuck, אביי himself offers a new way to fit זעירי and the ברייתא together. The difference is which kind of חטאת the blood came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer drops the fire-versus-sun split. Hardened blood may still be fit for the outer מזבח, so it stays 'blood' and one is liable. It is not fit for the inner service, so there it is pushed away and one is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: outer חטאות, whose blood goes on the outer מזבח in the courtyard
inner חטאות, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here אביי is talking to רבא.

phrases.english: Perhaps, surely,
here, with the outer חטאות,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא, which makes one liable.

phrases.english: there, with the inner חטאות!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא וַדַּאי, כָּאן בְּחַטָּאוֹת הַחִיצוֹנִיּוֹת, כָּאן בְּחַטָּאוֹת הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's silence in step 12, אביי offers a new answer to the contradiction from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by type of קרבן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After 'once pushed away, always pushed away', it seemed all congealed blood should be exempt, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Congealed blood of outer חטאות is not pushed away, so one is liable. Congealed blood of inner חטאות is pushed away, so one is exempt.

steps.title: רב חסדא proves the outer/inner split from the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבא recalls רב חסדא's ruling. Congealed blood of outer חטאות is still fit for 'taking and placing', so one is liable. Congealed blood of inner חטאות is not fit for 'dipping and sprinkling', so one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: You have reminded me of something that רב חסדא said. Blood of חטאות that congealed, and someone ate it, is liable, because the Torah says 'and he shall take and place', and this blood can be taken and placed. Blood of inner חטאות that congealed, and someone ate it, is exempt, because the Torah says 'and he shall dip and sprinkle', and this blood cannot be dipped into or sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up אביי's answer by quoting רב חסדא, who made exactly this split. He bases it on the different wording of the פסוקים for each type of חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For outer חטאות, the כהן takes the blood and places it on the מזבח, and even hard blood can be placed. So it was never pushed away and stays forbidden as blood. For inner חטאות, the כהן must dip his finger and sprinkle, which hard blood cannot do. So it is pushed away and loses the איסור of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: taking and placing, the blood service of the outer חטאת
dipping and sprinkling, the blood service of the inner חטאת
'the Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
fit for, able to have something done to it

steps.whatToRemember: Whether congealed blood is still 'blood' depends on whether it could still be used in its service. Outer חטאת blood (take and place) still works, so one is liable. Inner חטאת blood (dip and sprinkle) does not, so one is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the 'pushed away' principle depends on the exact service the Torah requires. The same hardened blood can be fit in one setting and unfit in another.

phrases.english: He said: You have reminded me of a matter
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking, now agreeing with אביי.

phrases.english: that רב חסדא said:
Blood of חטאות that congealed, and someone ate it, is liable,
'And he shall take and place,' the Torah says,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25

phrases.english: and it is fit for taking and placing.
Of the inner חטאות, and someone ate it, he is exempt,
'And he shall dip and sprinkle,' the Torah says,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:6

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי לָאו בַּר טְבִילָה וְהַזָּאָה הוּא.
phrases.english: and this is not fit for dipping and sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's outer/inner split from step 13 with an earlier ruling.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split between outer חטאות (liable) and inner חטאות (exempt) for congealed blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling, based on 'ולקח ונתן' (ויקרא 4:25) for outer חטאות and 'וטבל והזה' (ויקרא 4:6) for inner חטאות.

steps.title: רבא's own view: even congealed blood of inner sin offerings makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that eating congealed blood of inner חטאות still makes one liable, since that kind of blood is fit in outer חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא himself says: even with inner חטאות, if one ate the congealed blood he is liable, because the same kind of blood is fit for the מזבח in outer חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: After quoting רב חסדא's split, the גמרא tells us what רבא himself holds. He says one is liable even for congealed blood of inner חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא exempted inner חטאות because congealed blood cannot be used there for dipping and sprinkling. רבא looks at the type of blood instead of this specific offering. Congealed blood is fit in outer חטאות, so it still counts as real blood, and one is liable even when it comes from an inner חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Inner sin offerings, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל
Outer sin offerings, whose blood is placed on the outer מזבח
Its counterpart, the same kind of thing in a parallel case

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say congealed blood can be used for inner חטאות. He agrees it cannot. He only says that eating it still makes one liable, because the same kind of blood is fit in outer חטאות.

phrases.english: And Rava himself says:
Even with the inner sin offerings
and he ate it, he is liable,
since its counterpart is fit
in the outer sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's personal ruling, which disagrees with the רב חסדא split he just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating congealed blood makes one liable even from inner חטאות, since such blood is fit in outer חטאות.

steps.title: רב פפא extends this to congealed donkey blood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a conclusion from רבא: eating congealed donkey blood also makes one liable, since congealed blood is fit in outer חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: therefore, if donkey blood congealed and someone ate it, he is liable, because that kind of blood is fit in outer חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes רבא's reasoning one step further. Even blood from an animal that can never be brought as a קרבן counts, as long as congealed blood in general is fit somewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's test is not whether this specific blood could go on the מזבח. The test is whether this kind of blood (congealed) is ever fit. A donkey can never be a קרבן, yet congealed blood is fit in outer חטאות, so eating congealed donkey blood still makes one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a donkey, an animal never brought as a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא and רב פפא, congealed blood keeps the status of blood because congealed blood is fit in outer חטאות. This holds even when the specific blood could never reach the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore
blood of a donkey that congealed and he ate it, he is liable,
since its counterpart is fit in the outer sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's reasoning to a case further away, the blood of a non-קרבן animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating congealed donkey blood makes one liable, since congealed blood is fit in outer חטאות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Congealed blood is judged by its type, not by whether this particular blood could be offered.

steps.title: Blood on the body interposes whether moist or dry
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes זעירי: blood on the body is a חציצה in טבילה, whether it is moist or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of זעירי: blood, whether moist or dry, blocks the water during טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic that is also about blood. זעירי rules that blood on a person's body blocks the מקוה water in every state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טבילה to work, the water must touch the whole body. Anything stuck on the skin can block it. זעירי says blood counts as a blocker even while it is still moist, not only once it has dried.

keyTerms.meaning: Interposes, blocks the water from touching the body

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Ze'eiri said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּם, בֵּין לַח בֵּין יָבֵשׁ, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.english: Blood, whether moist or dry, interposes.
phrases.notes: This means it blocks during טבילה in a מקוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about blood, linked to the earlier discussion of blood in its different states.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood on the body is a חציצה for טבילה whether moist or dry.

steps.title: A ברייתא says moist blood does not interpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that blood, ink, honey and milk block only when dry. When moist, they do not block. This contradicts זעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: blood, ink, honey and milk block when dry. When moist, they do not block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges זעירי with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says moist blood does not block the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי said blood blocks even when moist. The ברייתא clearly says moist blood does not block. The two sources contradict each other directly.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Blood, ink, honey, and milk,
when dry, they interpose;
when moist, they do not interpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges זעירי's ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's ruling that moist blood is a חציצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says moist blood does not block, which contradicts זעירי.

steps.title: Sticking blood interposes; loose blood does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that זעירי means moist blood that sticks to the skin, and the ברייתא means moist blood that does not stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. זעירי speaks of blood that sticks to the skin. The ברייתא speaks of blood that does not stick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two sources are talking about different kinds of moist blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist blood that has started to thicken and cling to the skin acts like a real coating, so it blocks. Loose, runny blood washes away in the water, so it does not block. Both sources are now correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, the two sources do not really clash

steps.whatToRemember: For טבילה, blood blocks when dry. When moist, it blocks only if it sticks to the skin.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it sticks,
phrases.notes: "This" means זעירי's ruling.

phrases.english: that is where it does not stick.
phrases.notes: "That" means the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּסָרֵיךְ, הָא דְּלָא סָרֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source speaks of a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to disagree about whether moist blood blocks.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist blood that sticks blocks (זעירי). Moist blood that does not stick does not block (the ברייתא).

steps.title: Why does the verse say "you shall season"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the salt פסוק and asks what the word "תמלח" comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word "you shall salt" (תמלח): what does it come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק about salting the מנחה. It is setting up the next move by asking what the extra word "תמלח" adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says the מנחה is salted "with salt." So the verb "you shall salt" looks extra, and the גמרא wants to know its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall salt, from the פסוק about the מנחה
What does it come for, what does it teach

phrases.english: "You shall season": for what does it come?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier discussion of the salt פסוק, leaving the blood topics.

steps.title: The two words teach how to apply real salt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that each word blocks a mistake. "תמלח" teaches that תבונהו is not the way, and "במלח" teaches that salt water is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: had it said only "with salt," one might think תבונהו is required, so it says "you shall salt." Had it said only "you shall salt," one might think salt water is fine, so it says "with salt."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that shows why both words are needed. Each word rules out a wrong way of salting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "במלח" alone could suggest the method called תבונהו, which the גמרא explains later. "תמלח" corrects this. "תמלח" alone could allow salting with salt water, so "במלח" requires actual salt.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches, so the פסוק says
A method of salting that the גמרא explains later

phrases.english: For that which is taught:
"With salt": one might think tevonehu?
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this unusual word a little later, so don't worry about it yet.

phrases.english: The verse states: "You shall season."
If "you shall season," one might think with salt water?
The verse states: "With salt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about "תמלח" with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "תמלח" rules out תבונהו, and "במלח" rules out salt water. Both words are needed.

steps.title: "Do not omit salt": bring salt that never runs out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "ולא תשבית מלח" that one should bring salt that never stops, which is מלח סדומית.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall not omit salt": bring salt that never stops. Which is that? Salt of Sodom.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the next words of the פסוק. It reads "תשבית" as a hint to salt that "never stops," and identifies it as מלח סדומית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא connects the word תשבית to שובתת, meaning "stops." The salt that never stops, because it is always available, is מלח סדומית. That is the preferred salt for the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall omit, let it stop
Salt from the area of Sodom

phrases.english: "And you shall not omit salt":
bring salt that does not cease,
And which is this? Salt of Sodom.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְלֹא תַשְׁבִּית מֶלַח״ – הָבֵא מֶלַח שֶׁאֵינָהּ שׁוֹבֶתֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues expounding the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ideal salt for the מנחה is מלח סדומית.

steps.title: What if there is no Sodom salt?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that, without מלח סדומית, one may bring מלח איסתרוקנית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he did not find Sodom salt, he brings איסתרוקנית salt?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a source that a different kind of salt is acceptable when Sodom salt is not available. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the previous step named מלח סדומית, one might think no other salt works. The ברייתא wants a פסוק that allows a backup salt.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of salt dug out of rock

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא מֶלַח סְדוֹמִית
phrases.english: And from where is it derived that if he did not find salt of Sodom
he should bring salt of istrokanit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא מֶלַח סְדוֹמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the requirement of מלח סדומית has an alternative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a backup salt is valid when מלח סדומית is unavailable.

steps.title: "You shall offer": any salt, from anywhere, on שבת and in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: From "תקריב" the ברייתא learns that any kind of salt may be brought, from any place, even on שבת and even in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "you shall offer": offer any kind, offer from any place, offer even on שבת, offer even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word "תקריב" and draws four wide lessons from it. Salt for קרבנות is very flexible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "תקריב" widens the rule. Any salt works, including איסתרוקנית, and it may come from anywhere, even outside ארץ ישראל. Salting is done even on שבת and even in a state of טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: מלח סדומית is ideal, but because of "תקריב" any salt is valid. It may come from anywhere and is used even on שבת and in טומאה.

phrases.english: The verse states: "You shall offer":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

phrases.english: "you shall offer" any kind,
"you shall offer" from any place,
"you shall offer" even on Shabbat,
"you shall offer" even in impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a backup salt and adds three more lessons from the same word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "תקריב" teaches that any salt, from any place, may be brought, even on שבת and in טומאה.

steps.title: What does the word in the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unusual word תבונהו in the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of תבונהו?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא in step 21 used a strange word, תבונהו, and the גמרא now asks what it means. This question sets up a short back-and-forth among several אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know from step 21 that תבונהו is the wrong way to salt. But we do not yet know what that wrong way actually is. Before we can understand the rule, we need the word explained.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word in the ברייתא describing a wrong way of salting; its meaning is being asked about

phrases.english: What is “tevonehu”?
phrases.notes: This is the word from the ברייתא in step 21: תמלח teaches that תבונהו is not the way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the word תבונהו from the ברייתא in step 21 and asks for its meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word תבונהו in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Mixing salt in like straw in clay
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא says תבונהו means mixing lots of salt into the offering, the way straw is mixed into clay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: This is what it means: one might think he should mix it in like straw in clay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא explains the word by connecting it to תבן, straw. The idea is to work salt all through the offering like straw kneaded into clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He hears the word תבן (straw) inside תבונהו. So the mistake the פסוק blocks is a heavy mixing of salt all through the meat. The פסוק teaches that this is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He should mix it in like straw
One might have thought; it introduces an idea that will be rejected

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: הָכִי קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said: This is what it is saying:
One might think he should mix it in, like straw in clay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תבונהו comes from תבן: mixing salt into the offering like straw in clay.

steps.title: Then the word should have been different
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that if the meaning were mixing like straw, the ברייתא should have used the word יתבוננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, it should have said “yitabonenu”!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה בר עולא from the wording. If the meaning is straw-mixing, the ברייתא would have used the matching word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for straw-mixing is יתבוננו, but the ברייתא says תבונהו. Since the actual word does not fit, אביי says this explanation cannot be right.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If so,
it should have said “yitabonenu”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה בר עולא's explanation in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר עולא's reading of תבונהו as straw-mixing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word in the ברייתא does not match the form that straw-mixing would need.

steps.title: Piling salt layer upon layer like a building
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers his own reading: one might think the salt should be built up like a building, layer on layer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: One might think he should make it like a building.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבה בר עולא, אביי gives a new meaning. He connects the word to בנין, a building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea is now piling up salt in layers on the offering. The פסוק teaches that this too is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it brings in a new explanation in place of the rejected one

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
One might think he should make it like a building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 27 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תבונהו is connected to בנין: piling salt on in layers like a building.

steps.title: Then it should have said 'build it'
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if the meaning were building, the ברייתא should have said יבננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, it should have said “yivnenu”!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses the same kind of challenge on אביי that אביי used on רבה בר עולא. The wording does not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word for 'build it' is יבננו, not תבונהו. So the building idea also does not fit the actual word in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If so,
it should have said “yivnenu”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's explanation in step 28 in the same way as step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of תבונהו as building.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A building meaning would need the word יבננו, which the ברייתא does not use.

steps.title: Read the word in a different way
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא's word should be read as תְּבוּנֵהוּ (with an 'u' sound) instead of תְּבוֹנֵהוּ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: One might think “tevunehu.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not connect the word to straw or to building. He reads it a little differently, as תבונהו. That reading needs its own explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the word almost as it is and only changes how it is read. This avoids the wording problems of steps 27 and 29. Steps 31-32 explain what this new reading means.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא's reading of the word, with an 'u' sound; its meaning is explained in the next steps

steps.confusionAlert: The two words look almost the same in print. The earlier word is תְּבוֹנֵהוּ (with 'o'), and רבא's reading is תְּבוּנֵהוּ (with 'u'). Watch the vowel.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: One might think “tevunehu.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected explanation with a new reading of the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word should be read תְּבוּנֵהוּ (with 'u'), not תְּבוֹנֵהוּ.

steps.title: What does the new reading mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא's reading, תבונהו, means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is “tevunehu”?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gave a reading but did not explain it. So the גמרא asks what it means, setting up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new question, separate from step 25. It is about רבא's version of the word, not the original reading.

phrases.english: What is “tevunehu”?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבא's reading in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבא's reading תבונהו.

steps.title: Soaking the taste through, like understanding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains: one might think the salt must give its taste through the whole offering, as understanding fills a person. The פסוק says תמלח to teach otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: One might think he must put taste into it like understanding. The פסוק teaches: “You shall season.”
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי connects the word to בינה, understanding. The mistaken idea is that the salt must flavor the offering all the way through. The word תמלח shows that is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Understanding fills a person from the inside, so one might think the salt must also go all the way in. The פסוק's word תמלח teaches that a simple salting is enough. The next step shows what that salting looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; it introduces the word that answers the mistaken idea

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: יָכוֹל יִתֵּן בּוֹ
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: One might think he should put into it
taste, like understanding?
phrases.notes: He means the salt flavor would have to go all the way through the offering.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: “You shall season.”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: יָכוֹל יִתֵּן בּוֹ טַעַם כְּבִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 and ties it back to the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תבונהו means making the salt taste go through the whole offering, like understanding. תמלח teaches that this is not required.

steps.title: How the limb is actually salted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes the method: salt one side of the limb, turn it over, salt the other side, and bring it up to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He brings the limb and puts salt on it, then turns it over and puts salt on it, and brings it up.
steps.whatsHappening: After saying what is NOT needed, the ברייתא gives the practical method. Both sides get salted, and then the limb goes up to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the positive side of the rule. Salt on the outside surface, on both sides, is enough. No soaking through and no heavy layers are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb or piece of the offering
He brings it up (to the מזבח)

steps.whatToRemember: To salt a קרבן, put salt on one side of the limb, turn it over, salt the other side, and offer it. The salt does not need to go all the way through.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical standard for the מצוה of salting קרבנות and is the model for the next step.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He brings the limb and puts salt on it,
and then turns it over and puts salt on it,
and brings it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct method after step 32 ruled out the mistaken one.

steps.title: The same method for meat in a pot
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the same salting method works for meat before it goes into a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And the same is true for a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the method of salting a קרבן and applies it to the kitchen. Meat salted on both sides is ready for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary meat is salted to remove blood before cooking. אביי teaches that the קרבן method, salting both sides, is enough there too. It does not need to be soaked through or piled with salt.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: salting meat on both sides before cooking it in a pot is enough, just like salting a קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the Temple salting rule to everyday kashering of meat.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And the same is true for a pot.
phrases.notes: He means meat salted to remove its blood before it is cooked. Salting both sides is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the method of step 33 from קרבנות to ordinary cooking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting meat on both sides is enough before cooking it in a pot.
